Use case: stylized-concept. Create ONE portrait still illustration for a five-rank lofi focus-app growth world.
REFERENCE ROLES: Image 1 is the RANK 5 master for this SAME world's white circular plinth, camera, framing, soft pixel-painted material language, ivory/blue-gray/turquoise/pale-amber palette. Image 2 is supporting style reference only, do not copy any houses, town or shell.
Make a genuinely EARLIER physical growth form, not a fogged/hidden/cropped version of rank 5. The object itself must be simpler and smaller, with fewer cavities and less translucent ice. No buildings, village, structures, furniture, people, text, letters, numbers, labels, UI or watermarks. No shoreline/sea outside the object, no full natural landscape. Entirely self-contained on the white ceramic round plinth in a pure white empty space. Portrait image approximately 3:4. Keep the master image's plinth diameter, ellipse, location and camera exactly consistent: it spans about 88% of image width, bottom at 90% image height; fixed slightly elevated front-left three-quarter view. No camera zoom between ranks.
STYLE: detailed lofi pixel-painted miniature illustration, fine square color clusters with gentle painterly edges, softly shaded, intimate and quiet; avoid glossy photorealistic 3D, hard vector shapes, cartoon outlines or children's watercolor. Granular opaque white sugar is visibly distinct from smooth translucent blue ice. Use restrained soft daylight with warm pale-amber edge reflections and blue-gray shadows.
CURRENT RANK 1 — a single humble slightly chipped SUGAR CUBE, nothing else. Place it centered on the otherwise empty plinth, width about 34% of image width, base around 74% of image height. Its irregular near-cubic mass has a flat-ish top, squarish edges, and opaque coarse white sugar grains. A small shallow chip at the front lower corner exposes coarse granular sugar only; it is NOT a cave, tunnel or window. A few individual sugar grains and a modest little heap of powder lie directly below that chip, implying a soft granular trickling sound. This is recognizably ordinary sugar, not already an iceberg. NO blue transparent interior, NO cavity, NO water/puddles/droplets, NO icicles, NO birds, NO snowstorm, NO future-stage scenery. The rich master cavern should be completely absent. Keep visible tiny rough crystal facets and soft blue-gray contact shadows so the white cube reads against the white background. The simplicity should feel appealing and tactile, not a blank white geometric placeholder.

assets.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Asset: a single portrait game-world illustration, RANK 5 of a five-stage sugar-cube-to-ice-cavern growth sequence.
Image 1 is a STYLE AND PRESENTATION REFERENCE ONLY: match its intricate, softly pixel-painted lofi miniature scenery, granular square color clusters, quiet mood, white empty backdrop, low circular pale ceramic display plinth, elevated three-quarter camera. Do not copy its island, spiral, town, houses or sea.

Create a NEW self-contained miniature ice cavern grown out of ONE humble sugar cube. White portrait canvas, approximately 3:4. Keep the entire circular display plinth visible with modest margins; its ellipse spans about 88% of canvas width, centered horizontally, bottom at 90% of canvas height. Upper 22% of the canvas remains blank. The world occupies the lower central area, photographed/painted from a fixed elevated front-left three-quarter view.
RANK 5 completed form: a large irregular milk-white block has hollowed and transformed into a richly layered glacier grotto. Its broad open front clearly exposes a peaceful small turquoise underground lake, a few natural stepped ice shelves around and above it, translucent pale-blue ice columns and hanging icicles, and deeper connected alcoves visible through the opening. All of the lake stays INSIDE the cavern block; the outer ceramic plinth stays dry. Do not arrange a mountain in a spiral or make a tropical island. Keep a recognizable squared-off granular sugar cap at the back-left top, so the cube origin remains legible. The block outline is now sculptural and organically eroded, with the cutaway cave depth genuinely built into it, rather than decorative objects scattered around a cube.
A small daylight opening in the upper-right roof admits soft honey-colored sunlight that warms just a few ice edges and the entrance. Subtle reflected water light on the inner ceiling. Several small detached thin ice plates float apart on the lake and could gently touch with a crystalline clink. Three very small winter songbirds perch separately on a powder-snow shelf at the entrance; scenery dominates. Small snow particles near the roof opening, not a blizzard. No people.
Materials and style: crisp minute pixel-painted details, softly clustered mosaic brushwork in the same visual family as the reference, opaque powder snow transitioning to translucent layered ice, restrained bloom, pastel blue-gray, ivory, muted turquoise, pale amber reflections. Lofi, intimate, restful and softly magical. No cartoon outlines, no children's picture-book wash, no glossy photorealistic 3D render, no neon blue gemstones, no ornate palace, no buildings, no town, no lamps, no furniture, no text, no UI, no labels, no border, no watermark.
This is an illustrative still image, not an animation or diagram.
